newsitem.title: USA: Great Western may be seeking "white knight"--arbs.
newsitem.headline: Great Western may be seeking "white knight"--arbs.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp may be seeking a white knight to defend against H.F. Ahmanson and Co's $6 billion takeover bid, and Washington Mutual Savings Bank is a top candidate, arbitrageurs said Tuesday.
Ahmanson unveiled its unsolicited stock-swap proposal early this morning.
"Ahmanson's move looks very hostile and there are rumors of Washington Mutual emerging as a white knight," said an arbitrageur who declined to be identified.
Company spokesmen were not available for comment.
Another arb, who also declined to be named, said, "Everyone is saying Washington Mutual. For any of them (potential buyers of Great Western), it is tremendously accretive."
He added, "When you walk down the street (in California) there is a Great Western on the left and an Ahmanson on the right."

Because of this substantial overlap, he said, an Ahmanson-Great Western merger would result in many more office closings than the last huge financial services combination in California -- the 1996 combination of Wells Fargo and Co and First Interstate Bancorp.
"The amount of office closures would be substantial," the second arb said, noting that both Ahmanson and Great Western are based in the Los Angeles area.

Because Washington Mutual operates primarily in the U.S. Northwest, the potential savings from a deal with Great Western would not be as great as from Ahmanson's proposal, but the synergies are still compelling, arbitrageurs said.
Washington Mutual is a $47 billion Seattle-based holding company for Washington Savings Bank.
Ahmanson, the $50 billion parent of Home Savings of America, is the largest U.S. thrift. Great Western is the second largest, with $43 billion in assets.
Ahmanson is offering 1.05 of its shares for each Great Western share.
In midday New York Stock Exchange trade, Great Western shares were up nine points to 43-1/4, just below the session high of 43-3/4. Ahmanson shares were up 3-1/2 to 44.
Washington Mutual shares were up 7/8 to 56-1/16, just below a new year-high of 56-1/4 hit earlier in the day.
